query: Automotive display backlight units import tariff classification

statements.text: In HQ H026661, dated July 8, 2008, CBP classified an LCD display for auto/marine/industrial applications in heading 8531, HTSUS.
The tariff classification of automotive display unit from an unspecified country. Issued March 21, 2012 by U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

The subject module is intended for automotive use as a driver or passenger display screen. At importation, software on the subject PCB subassembly is described as capable of accepting, processing/converting, and displaying only video signals and backlight dimming level values generated from an automotive engine control unit (ECU).
the subject LCD display module is classified in heading 8528, specifically subheading 8528.59.25, HTSUS

In HQ H049555, dated April 13, 2009, CBP classified automotive LCD modules used as radio/message displays (to display time, velocity in miles per hour, climate control, compass, music controls, and Bluetooth connection status) in heading 8531, HTSUS.
Both LCD display modules are used in vehicle dashboards or HVAC system panels. They indicate the amount of fuel remaining in the tank, driving distance, time,
The specific information to be displayed is determined after importation, when the module’s PCB subassembly is programmed by the vehicle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).

This is in response to your ruling request of May 20, 2022, on behalf of Tianma America, Inc. (Tianma), pertaining to the classification of an automotive display module under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS).
Based on the foregoing, the subject display module falls outside the scope of heading 8524, HTSUS, as per Note 7 to Chapter 85.

CBP classified in heading 8531, HTSUS, a “Heads Up” automotive LCD display designed to provide limited, easily understood information ( i.e., speed, safety warnings, turn-by-turn directions, and audio settings) to the driver

The display module’s printed circuit board (PCB) subassembly contains a micro-controller unit, high-speed low voltage differential signaling (LVDS) deserializer integrated circuit (IC), decoder IC, light-emitting diode (LED) driver, voltage generators, and various resistors and capacitors that adhere to the bare board via surface-mount technology.
In NY N306705, dated October 31, 2019, CBP classified LCD indicator panels for automobiles in heading 8531, HTSUS.
